title: Adaptive binary prefix measurement gives a per-label common reconstruction estimate on correlated outputs

statement.quantifiers: Every pair of input states broadcast by ONE full-domain channel to two receivers with uniform halftrace error b; every finite tree depth L>=0.
statement.assertion: One EB pair map has EACH-label halftrace error<=Lb+sqrt(ln2/(2*2^L)), hence fidelity-affinity gap<=v(b)=O(sqrt(b log(1/b))).
assumptions: Uniform binary design prior; output tree states may be entangled or correlated.
Nonselective prefix measurements on other registers preserve chosen-register marginals.

inputs: Known pair, one broadcaster, depth L.
outputs: A single prefix POVM and posterior preparation for both labels; a dimension-free reference gap.
interface.precision: Finite depth exact inequalities, limit gives scalar zero-gap endpoint.
costs: Tree has 2^L systems and adaptive prefix outcomes; no efficient acquisition promise.
No arbitrary-family global EB channel follows from pair-specific reconstructions alone.

proof_mechanism: Iterated broadcaster marginals incur <=Lb by contractivity.
Helstrom conditional measurement and Pinsker give increment>=2E d_h^2.
Total binary record information<=ln2 selects one small increment.
P(h|x)=2p_h q_x yields the SAME per-label bound rather than an average-to-sup conversion.
EB fidelity monotonicity/affinity concavity and Powers-Stormer yield v(b).
obstructions: Multi-label rare probabilities break the special binary equality; no unrestricted all-family lift.

potential_uses.transfer_gate: Use pair gap only as a uniform scalar interface, and separately acquire the common entire-family reconstruction mechanism.

review.source_reported: Source reports internally reconstructed mathematics with scoped independent analytic audits; finite checks are not proof certification; no independent ingestion proof reconstruction, scientific replay, external correctness or priority clearance.
